title: Judge a Transaction by the Company It Keeps — Somya Rai & MD Sharique, EXL
talk_summary: EXL describes adding a graph neural network (GNN) over transaction/user/merchant edges to a fraud-detection pipeline, feeding GNN embeddings into the existing XGBoost model rather than replacing it, yielding ~27-33% relative TPR lift at fixed alert rate and 3ms P99 serving. The transferable engineering lessons are about leakage-by-construction, neighborhood-preserving sampling, multi-statistic aggregation, and caching precomputed embeddings to hit latency.

takeaways.technique: Leakage control by construction (disjoint time-split graphs)
takeaways.what_they_do: Each calendar month is its own disjoint graph with no cross-boundary edges, and every scalar/vocabulary is fit on the training month only then frozen, so train/val/test and future leakage are impossible by design rather than caught by post-hoc audit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each calendar month is its own disjoint graph. No edge overcrosses the boundary.

takeaways.technique: Multi-statistic aggregation instead of mean pooling
takeaways.what_they_do: When collapsing a variable-size neighbor set into a fixed vector, they concatenate mean, max, and std rather than averaging, because a single dangerous outlier gets diluted by mean pooling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Average those four together and you get 0.32. ... Take the max instead and it comes through untouched. 0.92.
takeaways.numbers: mean 0.32 vs max 0.92 on a 3-normal/1-fraud-ring example

takeaways.technique: Precompute and cache embeddings; keep per-request work O(1) in graph size
takeaways.what_they_do: They precompute per-layer representations for users/merchants offline into a low-latency store, then at request time only run the new transaction's own two-layer forward pass plus the classifier head, so nothing scaling with graph size runs per request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Nothing that scales with graph size runs per request.
takeaways.numbers: 2.3ms median, 3.1ms P99; footprint cut ~20x (60GB to 2-3GB) by caching only user/merchant embeddings

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of aggressive class-ratio downsampling that severs edges, they keep each selected user's full transaction history and never cap fraud users, handling imbalance downstream with balanced batch sampling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you trim a genuine user's history to hit a class ratio, you break the connectivity their neighbors depend on.
takeaways.numbers: training-time avg user degree 11.5-14 matches inference

takeaways.technique: Add a learned layer, keep the existing model as the head
takeaways.what_they_do: They did not replace XGBoost; the GNN produces embeddings that feed the same gradient-boosted model, isolating the gain to the added representation layer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We did not replace XG post. We fed it.
takeaways.numbers: 27-33% relative TPR lift over baseline at same alert rate

takeaways.technique: Pin math-library thread pools before heavy libraries load
takeaways.what_they_do: They pin math library thread pools to one before heavy libraries load, which alone cut latency dramatically, plus warm the model at startup so the first request isn't slow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We pin math library thread pulls to one before the heavy libraries even load. That alone is the difference between 30 milliseconds and one.
